title: Showing Your Attitude: Two Chilean Nobel Poets

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *lamentablemente*, *afortunadamente*, *indudablemente*, *en realidad*, *en rigor* and *precisamente* from B2 Unit 1. They stand outside the action and comment on the whole sentence: how sure, how glad or how exact you are. They are useful when you talk about writers, because you often correct a fact or show a feeling. Here they are used for Gabriela Mistral and Pablo Neruda.

sections.title: Stance adverbs in action
rows: En realidad, Gabriela Mistral se llamaba Lucila Godoy Alcayaga.
In fact, Gabriela Mistral was called Lucila Godoy Alcayaga. (you correct what someone may assume)
En rigor, Neruda no nació en Isla Negra, sino en Parral.
Strictly speaking, Neruda was not born in Isla Negra but in Parral. (the exact truth)
Lamentablemente, Mistral vivió muchos años lejos de Chile.
Unfortunately, Mistral lived many years far from Chile. (your feeling)
Precisamente en 1971 Neruda recibió el Nobel.
Precisely in 1971 Neruda received the Nobel Prize. (it points at the year)

items.spanish: Indudablemente, los dos poetas son muy leídos en Chile.
items.english: Undoubtedly, both poets are widely read in Chile.

items.spanish: Mistral, lamentablemente, murió lejos de su país.
items.english: Mistral, unfortunately, died far from her country.

items.spanish: Neruda, en realidad, tenía tres casas en Chile.
items.english: Neruda, in fact, had three houses in Chile.

sections.content: Use the comma test: if you can put commas around the adverb, it comments on the whole sentence. *Precisamente* takes no commas because it points at the word after it. Use one stance adverb per sentence.
